title: Show /limit-reset and let it offer resets whatever the client flag says
description: /limit-reset is hidden from the / menu, and the client only runs its reset flow when the tengu_cedar_ember flag is on: with the flag off the command is disabled, or falls through to the weekly session reset. This forces that flag's reader on and unhides the command, so /limit-reset always lists and runs as designed — it reads the account's resets, offers the next usable one in its confirm dialog, and only on Yes sends POST reset_rate_limits. Whether a reset is actually granted is still the server's call: an account it hasn't enabled gets ineligible (config_off) and nothing is used. Everything else the flag gates comes along too, as designed: at a usage limit the client reads the reset status and shows the /limit-reset offer in the limit notice. The claude.ai login check and the first-party, interactive-session checks are left as they are.

sites.description: /limit-reset's description getter picks the reset-card text when the cedar_ember gate is on. The call it tests is that gate, by definition — found through the text it selects rather than through the flag name, which only appears in a constant the reader consults indirectly.

`function ype(){return oSe().enabled===!0}` on 2.1.303: the one-line reader of the flag's enabled field. Every cedar_ember check goes through it — the command's isEnabled and description, its call, and the wall-time status read and offer in the rate-limit chunk, which import it — so forcing this declaration covers them all.
Its `isHidden: !0`, which keeps it out of the / menu even when enabled.
